scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom has been hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for about 50 years, and now she's too old to continue. We, her four kids, decided to take over the tradition by rotating. Each of us has hosted one holiday so far, and this Thanksgiving is my turn. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been close, and they live all over the country. This year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. Initially, it was just a sister trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet them there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York and went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I want to spend Thanksgiving with my wife's family, and it seems like a special opportunity. On the other hand, I agreed to take over hosting from my mom, and now I'm backing out, which is causing a lot of stress and anger among my siblings. I tried to find solutions, like paying for a rental spot or swapping with my brother, but it doesn't seem to be working out. I wonder if it's more about the tradition and what our mom wanted versus my personal desire to spend time with my wife's family. Is it wrong to prioritize my own family's wishes over the family tradition? Or is it more about communication and finding a balance that works for everyone? Maybe I should think about what's most important here. Is the tradition of hosting Thanksgiving more important than the opportunity for my wife and daughter to connect with their extended family? Or is it possible to find a compromise where both can be satisfied? It's also about respecting the wishes of our mom and the commitments we made as a family. I also need to consider how my actions are affecting my siblings. My oldest sister is really upset, and my brother doesn't seem too happy about the situation either. It's causing tension within the family, which is something I don't want. Maybe I should have communicated better from the start or found a way to make it work without disappointing everyone. In the end, I'm trying to do what's best for my family, but it seems like it's causing more problems than solutions. I'm not sure if I'm in the wrong or if there's a better way to handle this situation.
